meta.title: CERES-2 Y3 Launch visibility

jelly.viewers_title: Best views of the solid burns
jelly.pickup_note: At pickup the sunward ray grazes the ground, so the plume starts deep red. Clear sunlight: the ray passes at least 20 km above the surface. Lit S4 is a far fainter plume than the solid motors.
jelly.viewers_note: Sunlit S1–S3 only, sea-level sites. Bold: Sun at or below −6°, the darker sky. Dim: Sun already up.

notes: Pre-launch model, not telemetry and not an official ephemeris. T0 23:38:00 UTC (07:38 Beijing) is assumed: the launch is only reported as 'about 07:00 Beijing, 7 November' at the earliest.
CERES-2 Y3 (遥三), mission 砺锋行, is the second CERES-2 flight. Pad 95A is from secondary sources.

Public data: 100 t lift-off, 1.3 t to 500 km SSO, three solid stages and a liquid upper stage, 2.35 m core. The mission flies that 1.3 t. Motor loads, Isp and structure are scaled from CERES-1, whose published payload and lift-off mass the same model closes (validate_precedents.py).

Stage split 55.2 / 22.6 / 11.3 t of propellant, S4 load 1200 kg. Burn times 80 / 75 / 120 s and the S4 thrust 4.85 kN are assumptions; lift-off T/W 1.73. S4 climbs directly to the orbit in one 743 s burn, with no transfer coast and no second burn.

Steep S1 climb: a 116 km S1 impact from a 1.3 km/s burnout allows only a near-vertical path (the flat ballistic solution leaves S2 in the air). S2 then pitches over and yaws out the Earth-rotation velocity carried from the pad.

Zones: S1 and S2 are fitted to the centres of A5672 and A5673. S3 is aimed at 5450 km in the E4059 tail, because a direct S4 climb cannot close 1.3 t from the old mid-range aim. The orbit plane is an input, SSO i = 97.40 deg for 500 km, and those fits need at most 1.1 deg of S4 yaw to reach it, so the zones and an SSO plane agree. The fairing, 5 s after S2 burnout, lands in A5673 without being fitted.
LTDN 05:57: a dawn-dusk orbit, so the ground track runs close to the terminator. That is why this launch has a twilight plume at all.

Sunlight: geometric WGS84 occultation of the Sun's centre with DE440s, 30 s cadence. The 34' figure is the launch_jelly convention. Near pickup the ray grazes the ground, so the plume starts deep red; 'clear sunlight' means the ray passes at least 20 km above the surface.

On this page the zones' night edge follows the live Sun 0 line exactly, so it moves during playback; the area figures use one reference epoch, the sunlight pickup, as the static map does. Glow is an illustration. Plume size and brightness, weather, extinction and terrain are not modeled. Geometric visibility is not a claim of naked-eye detection; the S4 plume is far weaker than the solid motors.

The page's 500 km is the orbit-mean altitude; the osculating orbit at cutoff is 504 x 505 km. Shifting T0 keeps the Earth-fixed path and moves the Sun. Stage failure, as on the first flight, is not modeled. Data from GCAT (J. McDowell, planet4589.org/space/gcat).

zones.desc: Stage 2 falls at T+658 s and the fairing at T+1014 s; the zone is the union of CERES-2 Y1's A0118 and A0119
